Hi Zhengzheng,

 

Thanks for your interest in Canopy and sorry for my late reply – I’ve been traveling quite extensively. Please see my reply below:

 

1)      Yes, you can focus on meaningful genes/mutations which have different patterns across tissues. Also, I feel functional annotations helps pinpoint true somatic mutations (and this is especially helpful if you don’t have matched normal, in which case you may want to be sure the ones you called are true somatic mutations). Also this way your tree might be more meaningful in that all the point mutations that lie upon the tree branches are of functional impact.

2)      I am not sure what you showed in the picture is the correct output from sequenza but you may want to zoom out and focus on large and even chromosomal arm level CNA changes. There just seem to be way too many small segments as compared to our results from sequenza. Can you try zoom out and see what the results look like? At this stage, to avoid garbage-in-garbage-out, we feel large segments of CNA events with distinct patterns across samples/tissues should be those that are used as input.

 

Hope that this clarifies and let me know if you have more questions.

Yuchao
